title: Mom’s French Toast with Maple-Butter Syrup
description: Oval slices of French bread with crunchy crust edges, griddled golden, then topped with warm maple syrup with butter melted in and toasted walnuts or pecans.
author: Mom
story: Mom makes this with a loaf of French bread cut on the diagonal into ovals, so every piece has a crunchy crust edge. She never skips the nuts on top, usually walnuts or pecans.
imageAlt: Golden French toast slices with maple-butter syrup and toasted walnuts on a floral plate.

items: 1 loaf French bread (about 1 pound), a day old if you have it
2 to 3 tablespoons butter, for the griddle
½ cup walnuts or pecans, roughly chopped

steps.title: Cut the bread
steps.text: Slice the French bread on a sharp diagonal, about ¾ inch thick, to make long ovals.
steps.why: Cutting on the diagonal gives bigger slices, and every one keeps a strip of crust that turns crunchy on the griddle.

steps.title: Toast the nuts
steps.text: Toast the walnuts or pecans in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes, until fragrant. Tip them into a bowl.

steps.title: Make the custard
steps.text: In a shallow dish, whisk the eggs, milk, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, and salt until no streaks of egg remain.

steps.title: Dip
steps.text: Lay a few slices in the custard for about 20 seconds a side, until soaked but not falling apart.
steps.why: French bread is dense, so it needs a short soak to take in custard. Too long and the middle turns soggy.

steps.title: Griddle
steps.text: Melt a little butter on a griddle or large skillet over medium heat. Cook the slices 3 to 4 minutes a side, until deep golden and the crust edges are crisp. Add butter between batches, and keep finished slices warm in a 200°F oven.

steps.title: Warm the syrup
steps.text: Warm the maple syrup and butter in a small saucepan over low heat until the butter melts. Stir and keep it warm.
steps.why: Warm syrup holds the melted butter in, and it soaks into the toast instead of sitting on top.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pour the maple-butter syrup over the French toast and scatter the toasted nuts on top.
